checks.explanation: The claim is a verbatim quote from the source document describing the student's actions within a faculty team, piloting instructions, and receiving approval. The attribution to 'student' is accurate as the text uses 'I wrote'. No invented context or broadened category is present.

The label 'shared' is appropriate because the student explicitly states they worked 'On the faculty team' and 'wrote' instructions, indicating an individual contribution within collaborative work. The rationale correctly distinguishes this from 'led' (which requires explicit direction or sole ownership) and 'assisted'. The approval by the course lead does not negate the student's active role.

The label 'applied' is correct. The actions 'wrote' and 'piloted' describe applying established methods to complete a task (creating materials and testing them). There is no evidence in the text of designing new frameworks or adapting methods to specific constraints beyond standard piloting, so 'designed' or 'investigated' are not supported.

The label 'externally_reviewed' is supported by the phrase 'the course lead approved their use'. This constitutes an explicit external assessment of the work's quality and readiness. The rationale correctly identifies this as an external review rather than just a description or comparison.

The label 'adopted' is supported by the phrase 'approved their use in all sections'. This indicates actual use or adoption of the work by an organization (the faculty/course) across multiple sections. The rationale correctly links the approval to adoption.

The competency 'teaching_instruction' is supported. Writing lab instructions and piloting them constitutes planning and developing instructional materials, and testing with a section of students involves evaluating instruction for identified learners. The observed skill description matches the actions described in the source.

The competency 'programming' is unsupported. The source text mentions 'database lab instructions' but does not explicitly describe writing code, implementing a software system, or using programming languages like SQL for implementation. Writing documentation implies technical knowledge but does not demonstrate the explicit programming action required to support this competency. The rationale correctly notes the absence of explicit coding evidence.

The context 'database lab instructions' is a correct recognition of the tool/domain mentioned in the source text. It describes the specific instructional materials created. This does not claim mastery or depth, merely identifying the subject matter of the work.

The context 'faculty team' is a correct recognition of the domain/concept where the work was conducted. It identifies the collaborative environment without inventing institutional prestige or assuming specific roles beyond what is stated.

The context 'piloting' is a correct recognition of the concept/activity described in the source text. It identifies the testing phase mentioned by the student without inferring additional methodological depth.

The context 'course lead approval' is a correct recognition of the concept/event described in the source text. It identifies the external review mechanism mentioned without assuming its specific nature beyond what is stated.

dimensions.description: Individual contribution explicitly described in the evidence.

labels.assisted: Explicitly supported another contributor or followed guided work.
labels.shared: Explicit individual contribution within collaborative work.
labels.led: Explicitly directed the work or independently owned the deliverable; a title or possessive like my thesis alone is insufficient.

dimensions.description: Nature of the work demonstrated by the description, not prestige.

labels.unknown: A title, skill list, or credential alone does not describe the work.
labels.applied: Used established methods to implement or complete a described task.
labels.designed: Made and explained design choices or adapted methods to constraints.
labels.investigated: Investigated a question through an explicit method and analysis.

dimensions.description: How the work was evaluated; no implied ordering across disciplines.

labels.described: A concrete test, review, or assessment method is stated.
labels.compared: Evaluation includes explicit baselines, alternatives, or controls.
labels.externally_reviewed: External assessment is explicitly stated; this remains a claim until verified.

dimensions.description: Evidence describing results, separate from their independent verification.

labels.reported: A concrete outcome is reported without a measurement method.
labels.measured: An outcome and measurement method or comparison are stated.
labels.adopted: Actual use or adoption by identified users or an organization is stated.

category_guidance.project: Distinguish guided replication from individual design. Tool names do not establish depth. Preserve team contribution and ask about missing evaluation.
category_guidance.work: Assess described responsibilities and contributions. Employer reputation and job title do not establish ownership. Do not sum overlapping durations.
category_guidance.research: Unpublished research can demonstrate investigation. Evaluate methods and contribution independently of publication status; do not invent publications.
category_guidance.publication: Separate paper content, authorship, and review status. Do not rank unfamiliar venues or assume arXiv entails peer review. Request metadata verification later.
category_guidance.coursework: Preserve course and grade context. Enrollment alone does not establish mastery or independent implementation.
category_guidance.education: Preserve every degree and original grade scale separately. No prestige adjustment or invented grade conversion. Do not infer completion from attendance dates.
category_guidance.activity: Assess individual contribution in community, creative, leadership, and school activities without requiring technical work or publications.
category_guidance.other: Preserve unfamiliar evidence and uncertainty. Do not force it into a known technical competency or discard it because of taxonomy coverage.
